kept.title: Worktree claims guarded by atomic per-path lease (<wt>.lease, O_EXCL); stale only if pid dead AND aged >1h
kept.summary: createWorktree acquires a sidecar `<wt>.lease` file written with the 'wx' (O_EXCL) flag so the first writer wins and a racing second agent gets {contended:true, held} instead of a colliding `git worktree add`. A lease is reclaimable only when BOTH its owning pid is dead AND it has aged past ORCH_LEASE_STALE_MS (default 3600000 = 1h); same-pid is re-entrant. This is the concurrency primitive that prevents two agents corrupting one worktree path.

kept.title: gc-worktrees only removes clean + fully-merged-into-main + unregistered worktrees outside 24h retention; dry-run by default
kept.summary: The worktree GC sweep is conservative: it removes a worktree ONLY if it is clean (no uncommitted changes), fully merged into main, NOT registered/claimed, AND older than --retention-hours (default 24). Anything dirty, unmerged, or active is SKIP/NEEDS-ATTENTION. Runs dry-run unless --confirm is passed. Worktrees are ephemeral — durable value is merged code + recorded verdict.

kept.title: search_knowledge retrieval has a CI regression gate: recall@5 >= 0.85, MRR@5 >= 0.80
kept.summary: Retrieval quality is locked by test/retrieval-quality.test.js and scripts/retrieval-bench.js, which both fail if aggregate recall@5 drops below 0.85 or MRR@5 below 0.80 over the labeled query set. These exact thresholds are the contract for any change touching embedding/ranking.

kept.title: Notes are bitemporal: supersede stamps validTo and chains old<->new — history is NEVER deleted
kept.summary: record_decision(supersedes)/supersede_note stamp the old note invalid (validTo) and chain it to the new one rather than deleting. search_knowledge defaults to facts CURRENT now (superseded hidden), but as_of:<ISO> returns the fact current at that time and history:true returns the full timeline. Stale knowledge is retired, not removed — as-of reasoning depends on it.

kept.title: Write-time note dup guard rejects at title-vec cosine >= 0.70 — calibrated above same-subsystem p99 (0.66)
kept.summary: POST /overlay/note rejects a new note (ok:false, duplicate:true) if a current note has title-vec cosine >= DUP_THRESHOLD = 0.70. Calibrated: routine same-subsystem neighbours sit at p99~0.66 (0.55 would neuter the guard), dense clones cluster 0.68-0.88. The 0.55-0.70 band is left to the async dup-judge, not the write gate. Override with force:true or supersedes:.

kept.title: suggest_links flags a likely re-plan duplicate when an OPEN task overlaps at cosine >= 0.6
kept.summary: SUGGEST_DUP_THRESHOLD = 0.6 (distinct from the 0.70 note-write guard): high label/summary overlap with an already-OPEN task is surfaced as a probable replan duplicate so the planner supersedes instead of forking a near-identical task. Different number, different purpose — do not conflate the two dup thresholds.

kept.title: Forced ON-context was repeatedly net-negative in benchmarks (opus AND haiku) — opt-in is the deliberate design
kept.summary: v5-grounded and v5-haiku bench runs both landed NO-WIN: even with precise notes ON arms retrieved, ON did MORE output work than OFF (H_on 2,674 > H_off 2,023 on opus; gap persisted on haiku where weak-model hardness rose 3.7x). Value metric METRIC=(H_off-H_on)*5 - C, C=cache_read*0.1+cache_creation*1.25. Architectural lesson: context is opt-in, never force-injected.

kept.title: orch-gate enforces writes inside the claimed orch/attempt/* worktree; /tmp is NOT exempt; branch resolved from edit TARGET
kept.summary: The PreToolUse bash/edit gate blocks file writes unless they land on the task worktree branch (orch/attempt/*). /tmp and /private/tmp are explicitly NOT exempt (closes the cp-via-tmp bypass), and the branch is resolved from the edit TARGET worktree not the hook ambient cwd (fix a77e380) — so a subagent at session root on main still writes correctly into its worktree. Subagents must branch_task -> start_task before any write.

kept.title: Autowired context edges are born weight 0 + judged:false and only promote to weight>0 on a keep-verdict
kept.summary: Cosine autowire creates edges {by:autowire, judged:false, score:cosine} at weight 0; a promoted edge (weight>0) means the judge kept it. On restart, persisted promoted edges default to judged:true so tagBlindEdges does not re-stamp old kept edges as unjudged. Default explicit context-edge weight is 0.5 (DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WEIGHT). Edge weight encodes judge confidence, not mere existence.

kept.title: Competence harness self-invalidates (trustworthy:false) unless cold-rate is STRICTLY between 0 and 1
kept.summary: onboard-harness.js grades a cold agent vs a KB agent with control probes. A reading is trustworthy only when overall cold-rate is strictly in (0,1) — cold passing general controls but failing project probes. Cold-rate exactly 0 or 1 is reported DEGENERATE/NOT-TRUSTWORTHY (probes not independent of note wording — the earlier circular 0->100% keyword-graded bug). Also flags SUSPECT if cold passes <0.5 of controls.

kept.title: Try a few and pick is modeled as a problem -> attempts -> judge subtree, never a flat task
kept.summary: When the right approach is unknown, the planner must NOT create one flat task. It builds a problem node with multiple branch_task attempts resolved by a judge node, so the verdict is recorded as durable learning and losing approaches land in get_learnings().rejected[] — which future planner runs check to avoid relitigating a settled loss.

kept.title: Inline dashboard UI needs the daemon served over local HTTPS as a custom connector (ports 8787 / 8788)
kept.summary: Local stdio MCP servers do NOT render the inline MCP Apps UI — only a custom HTTPS connector does. Setup serves /mcp over locally-trusted HTTPS (mkcert) so the daemon can be added via Settings -> Connectors. Daemon runs HTTP on PORT 8787 (dashboard /graph) and HTTPS on 8788; the mkcert -install step needs a Keychain password and must be handed to the user.
